findings.reason: ncsi_rcv_rsp() (net/ncsi/ncsi-rsp.c:1165) is a packet_type handler registered with dev_add_pack() for ETH_P_NCSI on the NCSI-capable netdev (net/ncsi/ncsi-manage.c:1801-1803), so it receives raw skbs straight from __netif_receive_skb_core where only skb_reset_network_header(skb) was done (net/core/dev.c:5994) and no linearization is guaranteed. It casts the accessor result to struct ncsi_pkt_hdr * and dereferences hdr->type, hdr->id, hdr->length with no pskb_may_pull()/skb_linearize() anywhere in net/ncsi/ (verified: zero hits for pskb_may_pull/skb_linearize/skb_headlen/skb_is_nonlinear in the whole directory). Attacker-controlled length also flows on: payload = ntohs(hdr->length) feeds ncsi_validate_rsp_pkt(), whose pchecksum = (__be32 *)((void *)(h + 1) + payload - 4) dereferences up to 12+payload bytes past the network header with only an in-struct length equality as validation. Remote reachability needs a non-linear (frag/fraglist/GRO) NCSI frame, which requires a NIC doing scatter-gather receive of 0x88F8 frames; counterevidence is that most NCSI-capable drivers (e.g. ftgmac100, nfp) deliver linear RX skbs, so exploitability is unproven, and impact is an OOB read/crash rather than a proven UAF. Same pattern in ncsi_aen_handler() (net/ncsi/ncsi-aen.c:216-243) which dereferences h->type and validates checksum over sizeof(*h)+payload bytes with no pull.
findings.conclusion: NCSI packet_type handler ncsi_rcv_rsp() dereferences skb_network_header()-derived ncsi_pkt_hdr fields (type/id/length at ncsi-rsp.c:1185-1229) with no pskb_may_pull anywhere in net/ncsi, so a crafted non-linear 0x88F8 frame reads past skb_headlen into frags/stale head (OOB read, crash-prone).

findings.reason: ncsi_aen_handler() is the AEN branch of the same unguarded NCSI receive path (reached from ncsi_rcv_rsp() at net/ncsi/ncsi-rsp.c:1186). It casts skb_network_header(skb) to struct ncsi_aen_pkt_hdr * and reads h->type (lines 218, 226, 235, 243), then ncsi_validate_aen_pkt() computes pchecksum = (__be32 *)((void *)(h + 1) + payload - 4) and reads *pchecksum plus ncsi_calculate_checksum(h, sizeof(*h) + payload - 4), i.e. up to 24 attacker-influenced bytes beyond the header, all with no pskb_may_pull()/skb_linearize() in net/ncsi (zero grep hits). Same non-linear-reachability caveat as the rsp path.
findings.conclusion: ncsi_aen_handler() dereferences skb_network_header()-derived aen header fields and a payload-relative checksum pointer (ncsi-aen.c:216-243) with no linearization check, so a non-linear NCSI AEN frame reads beyond the skb linear area.

candidates.reason: ipv6_frag_rcv() calls pskb_may_pull(skb, skb_transport_offset(skb) + sizeof(struct frag_hdr)) at line 347-348 before taking fhdr = (struct frag_hdr *)skb_transport_header(skb) at line 354 and refetches hdr = ipv6_hdr(skb) after the pull; fragments are additionally reassembled via inet_frag_queue which linearizes the output.

xfrm_parse_spi() pskb_may_pull(skb, hlen) (line 171) covers exactly the ip_auth_hdr/ip_esp_hdr bytes before dereferencing skb_transport_header(skb) + offset/offset_seq at lines 175-176; the IPPROTO_COMP case also pulls sizeof(struct ip_comp_hdr) first.
hsr_fill_skb_info() and fill_frame_info() pskb_may_pull(skb, total_length) (lines 59, 69, 87, 103, 135, 714) before every skb_mac_header(skb) dereference in the receive/forward path.

nf_flow_offload_ip_hook()/ipv6 counterpart pskb_may_pull(skb, thoff + ctx->hdrsize) at lines 224/256/325/354/396/997/1022 before casting skb_network_header(skb) + offset to tcph/udph/greh/iph/ip6h; L2 branch also pulls skb_mac_offset + sizeof(vlan_ethhdr).
iptunnel_pmtud_check_icmpv6() pskb_may_pull(skb, skb_network_header(skb) + offset + 1 - skb->data) at line 407-408 before reading icmp6h->icmp6_type; also runs on the TX/encap path, not raw RX.

lowpan_rx dispatch dereferences *skb_network_header(skb) (a 1-byte dispatch read) at lines 68-72, 97, 114, 129, 145, 161, 177, 193, 264-265, 295-296 without any pskb_may_pull in this file; a single byte at skb->data is normally in the linear head for 802.15.4 frames, but whether a frag-list non-linear skb can reach lowpan_rcv() with an empty/short linear head was not traced in this run.
candidates.conclusion: Follow up: trace ieee802154 RX into lowpan_rx_h_dispatch/lowpan_frag_rcv to confirm whether skb_network_header(skb)[0] is guaranteed inside the linear head for every non-linear (fraglist) skb reaching net/ieee802154/6lowpan/rx.c.

candidates.reason: llsec_decrypt/llsec_encrypt compute data = skb_mac_header(skb) + skb->mac_len and scatter-list over skb_mac_header(skb), assoclen + datalen + authlen (lines 631, 675, 680, 857, 891, 894) with no pskb_may_pull in the file; the frame length comes from the received 802.15.4 PHY header, and whether the whole MAC frame is guaranteed linear (ieee802154 frames are typically small and linearly allocated) was not verified.
candidates.conclusion: Follow up: audit mac802154 ieee802154_rcv/llsec path to verify skb_mac_header(skb)..+frame_len always lies in the linear head (i.e. frames are never non-linear) before llsec scatter-list reads in net/mac802154/llsec.c.

candidates.reason: mctp_i2c_rx_thread/mctp i2c header handling casts (void *)skb_mac_header(skb) and reads header fields (mctp-i2c.c:499, 613; mctp-i3c.c:375, 520) with no pskb_may_pull visible; these skbs are locally allocated from the driver's own receive path so attacker control of linearity is doubtful, but the allocation path was not read.
candidates.conclusion: Follow up: read the mctp-i2c/i3c RX skb allocation to confirm the driver-built skb is always fully linear before the skb_mac_header() casts at drivers/net/mctp/mctp-i2c.c:499 and mctp-i3c.c:375.

candidates.reason: pppoe_disc_rcv/pppoe_rcv compute nhoff = skb_network_header(skb) - skb_mac_header(skb) and phdr = (struct pppoe_hdr *)skb_network_header(skb) (pppoe.c:1219-1239) with no pskb_may_pull in the function; pppoe is a bridged/ethernet-delivered protocol handler reachable by remote frames, but GRO/frag non-linearity of the header region for these small frames and the whole-function check were not completed.
candidates.conclusion: Follow up: verify whether a non-linear skb can reach pppoe_disc_rcv/pppoe_rcv with the 6-byte PPPoE header outside the linear head before the skb_network_header() casts at drivers/net/ppp/pppoe.c:1219-1239.

candidates.reason: sja1105_meta_unpack() reads skb_mac_header(skb) + ETH_HLEN .. +8 via packing() with no linear-length check in the function; callers in the tag rcv path were only skimmed and DSA-tagged frames may be non-linear when GRO merges them.
candidates.conclusion: Follow up: trace sja1105_rcv into sja1105_meta_unpack to check whether a GRO-merged non-linear meta frame can present its 8 payload bytes outside the linear head at net/dsa/tag_sja1105.c:105.

coverage_gaps: Only net/ and drivers/net/ .c files were scanned; the 145/82 per-file accessor hits were triaged by filename and receive-path heuristics, and ~230 files with 1-2 accessor uses (mostly TX checksum/GSO paths in ethernet drivers) were never opened.

net/ipv6/exthdrs.c, net/ipv6/ndisc.c, net/ipv6/mcast.c, net/xfrm/xfrm_iptfs.c, net/openvswitch/flow.c and net/core/drop_monitor.c have many accessor dereferences but were only name-triaged; the OVS flow-key extractor in particular walks variable-length headers and was not read.

The five unresolved candidates (6lowpan rx, mac802154 llsec, mctp i2c/i3c, pppoe, sja1105 tagger) were classified from accessor lines plus one-line context only; their enclosing receive functions and skb allocation/linearization provenance were not read.
limitations: Both findings are source-reading hypotheses, not reproductions: no KASAN build, crafted non-linear NCSI frame, or running NCSI device was used; unlike the phonet seed, the concrete failure is an OOB read past skb_headlen (or stale-head read after GRO realloc) rather than a KASAN-confirmed slab-use-after-free.

Exploitability of the NCSI findings depends on a driver that hands a non-linear skb for protocol 0x88F8 into __netif_receive_skb_core (scatter-gather/GRO RX with the NCSI ethertype); the survey of NCSI-capable drivers for this property was not done, so remote reachability is plausible but unproven.

The scan detected accessor lines but did not perform dataflow analysis, so a dereference reachable through a helper function or a macro-wrapped accessor (e.g. ipv6_hdr(), tcp_hdr(), ip_hdr() wrappers) could have been missed; those wrappers were outside this branch's literal grep terms.
